## In one sentence

Regression describes how an outcome changes with predictors while separating
systematic patterns from unexplained variation.

## Linear regression

A linear model can be written as:

$$
Y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_i + \varepsilon_i
$$

Here $\beta_1$ is the expected change in outcome per unit change in $X$ under
the model and covariate interpretation. Association is not automatically causal.

## Generalised linear models

A GLM combines a distribution for the outcome with a link function. Logistic
regression models a binary outcome through log-odds; Poisson regression models
counts through a log link. The link makes the linear predictor compatible with
the outcome scale.

## Diagnostics

Inspect residuals, leverage, influential observations, calibration, and whether
the mean-variance relationship is plausible. Validate predictions on data not
used to fit the model when prediction is the goal.

::: {.callout-tip}
Choose a model from the outcome-generating question, not only from the shape of
a scatterplot or the convenience of a software function.
:::

## Check your understanding

For a binary outcome, explain why ordinary linear regression may predict outside
$[0,1]$ and how a logistic model addresses that problem.
